To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the cool loops are coaligned with bright loops observed by SST and dark in AIA EUV channels starting form 335 A, (ii) only in AIA EUVA channel the computed level recombination continua is in agreement with observations, while the synthetic continua are much too low in other channels, (iii) the surplus emission in AIA channels is due to numerous hot and faint loops in front, and (iv) the standard absorption model fails in describing the dark loop brightness
the continuum of cool flare loops observed in the EUV by AIA cannot be explained by recombination continua alone and that the standard absorption model fails to describe the dark loop brightness.

(1) the dark loop structures in AIA 335-94 A channels are not due to recombination continua, but rather to numerous faint EUV lines emitted by hot loops in front of them; (2) the standard absorption model fails when applied to cool loops, because it does not take into account the presence of the continuum.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how much of the EUV signal in AIA images is due to the continuum radiation and how much is due to the line emission.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cool loop emission in AIA 171 A and 193 A is not due to recombination continua of hydrogen and helium, respectively.
the dark loops observed in the 335 A channel are indeed cool, but in other channels they might be contaminated by emission from hotter but fainter loops.
the dark loops in the 335-94 A channels of AIA are not due to the recombination continua of hydrogen and helium, but to a combination of numerous EUV lines and recombination continua.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the standard absorption model is not sufficient to explain the observed dark loop brightness and that the recombination continuum is not the only mechanism responsible for the observed darkening of the loops.
the cool loops observed in this flare are dark because they are cool, and the continuum is not the main reason of the dark loop appearance.
the cool loops observed during the gradual phase are not dark due to recombination continua.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cool loops are not dark in all AIA channels, and that their appearance depends on the relative level of continuum and lines in a given channel.
the standard absorption model is not applicable to cool loops observed by SDA/AIA in the EUV channels.
in the cool loop observations of flares one needs to consider not only recombination continua but also the presence of numerous fainter EUV loops.
